intro-1.text: This is MathLive 2.0, the Obsidian plugin for math notes, now with less typing and more scanning.

editing-1.text: Click any formula in your note and start typing. A fraction appears right there, as you write it, in place.

editing-2.text: The formula reads as finished math, and the note's source stays plain LaTeX. Nothing proprietary, nothing locked in.

ai-fill-1.text: New in 2.0 is the sparkle button. Click it next to a formula, and you can scan from the clipboard or the screen.

ai-fill-2.text: Choose clipboard image. A progress notice says it's reading the formula, and then the equation fills in, ready to edit.

scan-screen-1.text: Say a lecture PDF is open beside your note. Choose scan from screen, and the whole screen dims.

scan-screen-2.text: Drag a box around any formula in the PDF. It lands in your note as editable math.

scan-screen-3.text: It's just a formula like any other, so you can click in and fix a symbol or change a term.

pdf-notes-1.text: To bring in a whole document, right-click the PDF and choose Convert to notes with MathLive. The dialog shows the page count.

pdf-notes-2.text: Click Convert, and the dialog counts pages as they're read. Blank pages are skipped and not charged.

pdf-notes-3.text: The new note opens with each page as Markdown and editable LaTeX, and every page links back to its place in the PDF.

connect-1.text: Getting started is easy. Your first three scans are a free trial, and you don't need an account.

connect-2.text: When the trial scans are used up, a dialog offers Connect. Click it, and it says to finish in your browser.

connect-3.text: The MathLive website opens. Sign in with Google, and that's it. There are no API keys to copy.

connect-4.text: Back in Obsidian, a notice says MathLive is connected, and the scan that was waiting finishes on its own.

website-1.text: There's also a new website, at mathlive.danz.blog, with an account page for your plan, scans left, and connected devices.

website-2.text: Plans are simple. Free, Monthly at four dollars a month, or Lifetime at forty-nine dollars, once. Typing and editing formulas stay free forever.

reliable-1.text: Scans run on hosted vision models, with automatic failover to a second provider. You're only charged when a scan returns a result.

outro-1.text: Get MathLive 2.0 from Community plugins in Obsidian. Search for MathLive, or visit mathlive.danz.blog to learn more.
